learning_objective: 🎯 Understand the delicate web of life! Explore how energy flows through food chains, and how human activities impact the protective ozone layer and waste management.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: An ecosystem consists of Biotic components (living things like plants, animals, microbes) interacting with Abiotic components (non-living things like soil, water, sunlight, temperature).
A food chain shows 'who eats whom' (Producer → Primary Consumer → Secondary Consumer). A network of interconnected food chains is a Food Web, which provides stability to the ecosystem.

Energy flows in only ONE direction (unidirectional). According to the 10% Law, only 10% of the energy is transferred from one trophic level to the next. The rest (90%) is lost as heat. This is why food chains rarely exceed 4 or 5 steps.

Harmful non-biodegradable chemicals (like pesticides/DDT) enter the food chain and their concentration increases at each successive trophic level. Human beings (top carnivores) accumulate the highest amount of these toxins.

Ozone (O₃) forms a protective shield in the stratosphere, blocking harmful UV radiation from the sun. Synthetic chemicals called CFCs (Chlorofluorocarbons, used in old fridges) destroy ozone molecules, causing 'holes' in the layer.

fun_activity.title: 🗑️ The Waste Audit
fun_activity.instructions: Look at the dustbin in your kitchen. Categorize the waste into 'Biodegradable' (vegetable peels, paper) and 'Non-Biodegradable' (plastic wrappers, batteries). Imagine where each item will be in 100 years!

exam_tips: 📌 Always draw the energy flow pyramid upright, with Producers at the wide base.
📌 Know the difference between Ozone at the ground level (it's a deadly poison) and Ozone in the stratosphere (it's a life-saving shield).
📌 The 10% Law calculation: If a plant has 10,000 Joules of energy, the deer gets 1,000J, and the lion gets only 100J.
quick_recap: ⭐ Producers (Autotrophs) capture only about 1% of the sunlight energy falling on their leaves to make food.
⭐ Decomposers (bacteria/fungi) are the 'cleaners' of the ecosystem, returning nutrients back to the soil.
⭐ Managing garbage disposal (segregation, recycling, composting) is critical to protect our environment.
